```{r}
# Outboard engine sales trend data come from the National Marine Manufacturers Association. They publish a U.S. Recreational Boating Statistical Abstract annually. The pdf can be dowloaded from [here](https://www.nmma.org/statistics/publications/statistical-abstract). You must create an account in order to download the pdfs. For this report, the pdf has been downloaded and saved to the data/unformatted folder.

# We will start by extracting all the relevant data, then will summarize to make an indicator.

file_path <- here("data/unformatted/2024 Outboard Engine Sales Trends.pdf")

# First I need a function to scrape the data from any of the tables in the pdf. This function will scrape annual sales data from the Gulf states. Luckily the tables seem to always be in a consistent format.

# Function to extract state-specific outboard sales by page/table
extract_hp_data <- function(file_path, page_num) {
  
  #suppress warning here about the font (not necessary)
  pdf_text_raw <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(pdftools::pdf_text(file_path)[page_num]))
  lines <- str_split(pdf_text_raw, "\\n")[[1]]
  lines <- str_trim(lines)
  
  # 1. Title Extraction
  title_line <- lines[str_detect(lines, "^Table \\d+:")]
  if(length(title_line) > 0) {
    clean_title <- str_match(title_line[1], ":\\s*(.*?)\\s*unit sales")[,2]
  } else {
    clean_title <- paste("Segment_Page", page_num)
  }
  
  target_states <- c("Alabama", "Florida", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Texas")
  
  scrape_row <- function(state_name) {
    # 2. Targeted Regex: Starts with state name and ends with numeric rank
    pattern <- paste0("^[\"\\s]*", state_name, ".*\\d$")
    row_text <- lines[str_detect(lines, pattern)]
    
    # Fallback if rank column is missing or text layout is slightly shifted
    if(length(row_text) == 0) {
       pattern <- paste0("^[\"\\s]*", state_name)
       potential_rows <- lines[str_detect(lines, pattern)]
       if(length(potential_rows) == 0) return(rep(NA, 14))
       # Take the longest matching line (likely the table row)
       row_text <- potential_rows[which.max(nchar(potential_rows))]
    }
    
    # 3. Handling Dashes and Numbers
    # Remove state name from the start to avoid numeric interference
    just_data_text <- str_remove(row_text, paste0("^[\"\\s]*", state_name))
    
    # 4. Handle Unicode Em-dashes and Numbers
    # Regex for: 
    # (a) Numbers/Commas: -?[\\d,.]+
    # (b) Unicode Dash Placeholders: [\u2014\u2013]
    values <- str_extract_all(just_data_text, "-?[\\d,.]+|[\u2014\u2013]")[[1]]
    
    # Convert to numeric or NA
    clean_vals <- sapply(values, function(x) {
      # If it's a dash or hyphen, it's missing data for that year
      if (x %in% c("\u2014", "\u2013", "-")) return(NA)
      # Otherwise clean commas and convert to numeric
      return(as.numeric(gsub(",", "", x)))
    })
    
    # Remove the string labels
    numeric_vals <- unname(clean_vals)
    
    # 4. Return 2011-2024 (the first 14 columns of data)
    if(length(numeric_vals) >= 14) {
      return(as.numeric(numeric_vals[1:14]))
    } else {
      # If for some reason the row is short, pad with NA
      return(as.numeric(c(numeric_vals, rep(NA, 14 - length(numeric_vals)))))
    }
  }
  
  data_list <- lapply(target_states, scrape_row)
  names(data_list) <- target_states
  
  df <- data.frame(
    year = 2011:2024,
    Texas = data_list$Texas,
    Louisiana = data_list$Louisiana,
    Mississippi = data_list$Mississippi,
    Alabama = data_list$Alabama,
    Florida = data_list$Florida
  )
  
  return(list(name = clean_title, data = df))
}


# Now we will use this function to extract sales data for all the different engine sizes.There are 10 tables ranging from 4hp engine sales to 300+hp. 

#The tables are on every other page starting on page 21 for the 2024 report.
page_numbers = seq(21,41, by=2)

hp_data_list <- list()

for (p in page_numbers) {
  tryCatch({
    result <- extract_hp_data(file_path, p)
    hp_data_list[[result$name]] <- result$data
    message("Successfully scraped: ", result$name)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Error on page ", p, ": ", e$message)
  })
}

```

```{r}
#Now that we've scraped the data from all the relevant tables, we want to combine the information into an indicator. We will combine all Gulf states and just look at three categories of engine sizes. Small = Less than 30hp, Medium = 30-149.9hp, Large = 150+hp. 

# Define the mapping of HP ranges to Categories
category_map <- list(
  "Inshore"    = c("Less than 4 hp", "4–9.9 hp", "10–29.9 hp", "30–49.9 hp"),
  "Nearshore" = c("50–74.9 hp", "75–99.9 hp", "100–149.9 hp"),
  "Near-offshore"   = c("150–199.9 hp", "200–249.9 hp", "250–299.9 hp"),
  "Far-offshore" = c("300 hp and greater")
)

# Process the list into 4-column table
outboard_summary <- hp_data_list %>%
  # Convert list of dataframes into one long dataframe
  imap_dfr(~ .x %>% mutate(segment = .y)) %>%
  # Create the new category labels
  mutate(category = case_when(
    segment %in% category_map[["Inshore"]]    ~ "Inshore",
    segment %in% category_map[["Nearshore"]] ~ "Nearshore",
    segment %in% category_map[["Near-offshore"]]   ~ "Near-offshore",
    segment %in% category_map[["Far-offshore"]]   ~ "Far-offshore"
  )) %>%
  # Row-wise sum of the 5 states, then group-wise sum by category
  mutate(five_state_total = Texas + Louisiana + Mississippi + Alabama + Florida) %>%
  group_by(year, category) %>%
  summarise(total_sales = sum(five_state_total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Pivot to wide format to match your requested column structure
  pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = total_sales) %>%
  # Ensure columns are in the specific order you requested
  select(year, `Inshore`, `Nearshore`, `Near-offshore`, `Far-offshore`)

head(outboard_summary)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Map each list element (HP category) to an estimated HP midpoint
hp_midpoints <- c(
  "Less than 4 hp"      = 2.5,
  "4–9.9 hp"           = 7.0,
  "10–29.9 hp"         = 20.0,
  "30–49.9 hp"         = 40.0,
  "50–74.9 hp"         = 62.5,
  "75–99.9 hp"         = 87.5,
  "100–149.9 hp"       = 125.0,
  "150–199.9 hp"       = 175.0,
  "200–249.9 hp"       = 225.0,
  "250–299.9 hp"       = 275.0,
  "300 hp and greater" = 350.0  # Conservative estimate for 300+ class
)

# 2. Combine list into a single long-format data frame
hp_df_long <- imap_dfr(hp_data_list, ~ .x %>% 
  mutate(hp_category = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida"),
    names_to = "state",
    values_to = "sales"
  )

# 3. Apply physics-based area relationship
# Model Assumptions:
# Speed (knots) approx = 3.5 * sqrt(HP)
# Travel time budget = 2 hours one-way -> Radius (nm) = Speed * 2
# Area (nm^2) = 0.5 * pi * Radius^2
hp_analysis <- hp_df_long %>%
  mutate(
    hp_midpoint = hp_midpoints[hp_category],
    
    # Total HP sold in that bucket
    total_hp_sold = sales * hp_midpoint,
    
    # Reachable Radius (nm) for a 2-hour trip at estimated cruising speed
    est_speed_knots = 3.5 * sqrt(hp_midpoint),
    est_radius_nm   = est_speed_knots * 2,
    
    # Accessible Area per engine (nm^2)
    area_per_engine = 0.5 * pi * (est_radius_nm^2),
    
    # Total potential spatial footprint added by this batch of engines
    total_potential_area = sales * area_per_engine
  )

# 4. Summarize by State and Year
state_yearly_summary <- hp_analysis %>%
  group_by(year, state) %>%
  summarize(
    total_engines_sold = sum(sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_hp_added     = sum(total_hp_sold, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_area_index   = sum(total_potential_area, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, # Millions nm^2
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 5. Summarize Gulf-wide totals per Year
gulf_yearly_summary <- state_yearly_summary %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    total_hp_added   = sum(total_hp_added),
    total_area_index = sum(total_area_index)
  )
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load Midpoints & Calculate Yearly Added Area (from previous step) ---
hp_midpoints <- c(
  "Less than 4 hp"      = 2.5,
  "4–9.9 hp"           = 7.0,
  "10–29.9 hp"         = 20.0,
  "30–49.9 hp"         = 40.0,
  "50–74.9 hp"         = 62.5,
  "75–99.9 hp"         = 87.5,
  "100–149.9 hp"       = 125.0,
  "150–199.9 hp"       = 175.0,
  "200–249.9 hp"       = 225.0,
  "250–299.9 hp"       = 275.0,
  "300 hp and greater" = 350.0
)

# Parse data and compute yearly added area per state
hp_yearly_added <- imap_dfr(hp_data_list, ~ .x %>% mutate(hp_category = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida"),
               names_to = "state", values_to = "sales") %>%
  mutate(
    hp_midpoint = hp_midpoints[hp_category],
    est_speed_knots = 3.5 * sqrt(hp_midpoint),
    est_radius_nm   = est_speed_knots * 2,
    area_per_engine = 0.5 * pi * (est_radius_nm^2),
    added_area      = sales * area_per_engine / 1e6 # Millions nm^2
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, state) %>%
  summarize(added_area = sum(added_area, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# --- 2. Calculate Active Fleet Area Footprint with Decay ---
# Annual survival rate (e.g., 90% active year-over-year, 10% attrition)
annual_survival_rate <- 0.90 

calculate_active_fleet <- function(df, survival_rate = 0.90) {
  df <- df %>% arrange(year)
  years <- unique(df$year)
  states <- unique(df$state)
  
  results <- list()
  
  for (s in states) {
    state_data <- df %>% filter(state == s)
    active_area <- numeric(nrow(state_data))
    
    current_stock <- 0
    for (i in seq_along(state_data$year)) {
      # Current active stock = remaining old stock * survival_rate + new engines added
      current_stock <- (current_stock * survival_rate) + state_data$added_area[i]
      active_area[i] <- current_stock
    }
    
    state_data$active_area_index <- active_area
    results[[s]] <- state_data
  }
  
  bind_rows(results)
}

active_fleet_summary <- calculate_active_fleet(hp_yearly_added, survival_rate = 0.90)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Map each list element (HP category) to an estimated HP midpoint
hp_midpoints <- c(
  "Less than 4 hp"      = 2.5,
  "4–9.9 hp"           = 7.0,
  "10–29.9 hp"         = 20.0,
  "30–49.9 hp"         = 40.0,
  "50–74.9 hp"         = 62.5,
  "75–99.9 hp"         = 87.5,
  "100–149.9 hp"       = 125.0,
  "150–199.9 hp"       = 175.0,
  "200–249.9 hp"       = 225.0,
  "250–299.9 hp"       = 275.0,
  "300 hp and greater" = 350.0
)

# 2. Combine list into long format & apply physics-based area calculation
hp_df_long <- imap_dfr(hp_data_list, ~ .x %>% mutate(hp_category = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida"),
    names_to = "state",
    values_to = "sales"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Apply 50/50 Florida split: Allocate 50% of FL sales to the Gulf Coast
    gulf_sales = if_else(state == "Florida", sales * 0.50, sales),
    
    # Physics & Range Model
    hp_midpoint     = hp_midpoints[hp_category],
    est_speed_knots = 3.5 * sqrt(hp_midpoint),
    est_radius_nm   = est_speed_knots * 2,         # 2-hour travel radius
    area_per_engine = 0.5 * pi * (est_radius_nm^2), # Semi-circle accessible area (nm^2)
    
    # Yearly Gulf area added by category
    added_gulf_area = gulf_sales * area_per_engine / 1e6 # Millions nm^2
  )

# 3. Aggregate yearly added area per state (Gulf Coast only)
yearly_added_by_state <- hp_df_long %>%
  group_by(year, state) %>%
  summarize(
    gulf_sales_total = sum(gulf_sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    added_area_index = sum(added_gulf_area, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Apply 10% Annual Engine Attrition / Survival Model (90% survival rate)
calculate_active_gulf_fleet <- function(df, survival_rate = 0.90) {
  states <- unique(df$state)
  results <- list()
  
  for (s in states) {
    state_data <- df %>% filter(state == s) %>% arrange(year)
    active_area <- numeric(nrow(state_data))
    
    current_stock <- 0
    for (i in seq_along(state_data$year)) {
      # Current active stock = (previous stock * survival_rate) + new engines added
      current_stock <- (current_stock * survival_rate) + state_data$added_area_index[i]
      active_area[i] <- current_stock
    }
    
    state_data$active_area_index <- active_area
    results[[s]] <- state_data
  }
  
  bind_rows(results)
}

# Run active fleet model
active_gulf_fleet <- calculate_active_gulf_fleet(yearly_added_by_state, survival_rate = 0.90)

# Optional: Relabel Florida for clarity in plots
active_gulf_fleet <- active_gulf_fleet %>%
  mutate(state_label = if_else(state == "Florida", "Florida (50% Gulf)", state))
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggspatial)
library(nmfspalette)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fetch Official Gulf of Mexico Ocean Polygon via Web Service
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
target_crs <- 5070 

# Direct GeoJSON / WFS query to MarineRegions.org for Gulf of Mexico (IHO Sea Area ID 26)
gulf_url <- "https://geo.vliz.be/geoserver/wfs?request=getFeature&service=wfs&version=1.1.0&typename=MarineRegions:iho&cql_filter=id=26&outputFormat=json"
gulf_ocean_poly <- st_read(gulf_url, quiet = TRUE) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = target_crs)

# Load state boundaries
states <- ne_states(country = "United States of America", returnclass = "sf")
gulf_states <- states %>%
  filter(name %in% c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida", "Georgia")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = target_crs)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate Milestone Distances & Intersect directly with Ocean Polygon
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
hp_midpoints <- c(
  "Less than 4 hp"      = 2.5,   "4–9.9 hp"           = 7.0,
  "10–29.9 hp"         = 20.0,  "30–49.9 hp"         = 40.0,
  "50–74.9 hp"         = 62.5,  "75–99.9 hp"         = 87.5,
  "100–149.9 hp"       = 125.0, "150–199.9 hp"       = 175.0,
  "200–249.9 hp"       = 225.0, "250–299.9 hp"       = 275.0,
  "300 hp and greater" = 350.0
)

hp_df <- imap_dfr(hp_data_list, ~ .x %>% mutate(hp_category = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida"),
               names_to = "state", values_to = "sales") %>%
  mutate(
    gulf_sales  = if_else(state == "Florida", sales * 0.50, sales),
    hp_midpoint = hp_midpoints[hp_category],
    speed_knots = 3.5 * sqrt(hp_midpoint),
    radius_nm   = speed_knots * 2
  )

milestone_years <- c(2011, 2016, 2021, 2024)

# Filter for Near-offshore & Far-offshore engines only (>= 150 HP)
reach_milestones_offshore <- hp_df %>%
  filter(
    year %in% milestone_years,
    hp_midpoint >= 175  # 150–199.9 HP class and above
  ) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(
    # Average reach radius specifically for the offshore-capable fleet
    avg_reach_nm = sum(radius_nm * gulf_sales, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(gulf_sales, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(year))

nm_to_m <- 1852

# Create buffers and clip against the Official Gulf Ocean Polygon
buffers_df <- map_dfr(1:nrow(reach_milestones), function(i) {
  yr <- reach_milestones$year[i]
  dist_m <- reach_milestones$avg_reach_nm[i] * nm_to_m
  
  # 1. Buffer land
  buf <- st_buffer(st_union(gulf_states), dist = dist_m)
  
  # 2. Subtract land
  buf_offshore <- st_difference(buf, st_union(gulf_states))
  
  # 3. Intersect ONLY inside official Gulf of Mexico ocean waters
  buf_gulf_only <- st_intersection(buf_offshore, gulf_ocean_poly)
  
  st_sf(
    year = as.factor(yr),
    radius_nm = round(reach_milestones$avg_reach_nm[i], 1),
    geometry = st_geometry(buf_gulf_only)
  )
})

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot Map
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#e0f2f1")) +
  
  # Draw clean buffer bands clipped strictly to official Gulf ocean boundary
  geom_sf(data = buffers_df, aes(fill = year), color = "gray30", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_sf(data = gulf_states, fill = "#f4f4f2", color = "gray40", size = 0.4) +
  
  scale_fill_nmfs(
    palette = "complement_teal", 
    discrete = TRUE, 
    reverse = FALSE,
    name = "Milestone Year\n(2-Hr Reach Radius)"
  ) +
  
  # View Bounding Box
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-97.5, -81.0), 
    ylim = c(24.5, 31.0), 
    crs = st_crs(4326), 
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Shifted Scale Bar & North Arrow to Bottom Right (br)
  annotation_scale(
    location = "br", 
    width_hint = 0.25,
    pad_x = unit(1, "in"), 
    pad_y = unit(0.3, "in")
  ) +
  annotation_north_arrow(
    location = "br", 
    which_north = "true", 
    pad_x = unit(1, "in"), 
    pad_y = unit(0.5, "in"),
    style = north_arrow_minimal()
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Expansion of Average Offshore Reach in the Gulf",
    subtitle = "Modeled 2-hour single-trip radius based on outboard horsepower trends",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "white", size = 0.2)
  )
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggspatial)
library(nmfspalette)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Fetch Official Gulf of Mexico Ocean Polygon via Web Service
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
target_crs <- 5070 

# Direct GeoJSON / WFS query to MarineRegions.org for Gulf of Mexico (IHO Sea Area ID 26)
gulf_url <- "https://geo.vliz.be/geoserver/wfs?request=getFeature&service=wfs&version=1.1.0&typename=MarineRegions:iho&cql_filter=id=26&outputFormat=json"
gulf_ocean_poly <- st_read(gulf_url, quiet = TRUE) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = target_crs)

# Load state boundaries individually
states <- ne_states(country = "United States of America", returnclass = "sf")
gulf_states <- states %>%
  filter(name %in% c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida", "Georgia")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = target_crs)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate State-Specific Milestone Distances & Generate Custom Buffers
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
hp_midpoints <- c(
  "Less than 4 hp"      = 2.5,   "4–9.9 hp"           = 7.0,
  "10–29.9 hp"         = 20.0,  "30–49.9 hp"         = 40.0,
  "50–74.9 hp"         = 62.5,  "75–99.9 hp"         = 87.5,
  "100–149.9 hp"       = 125.0, "150–199.9 hp"       = 175.0,
  "200–249.9 hp"       = 225.0, "250–299.9 hp"       = 275.0,
  "300 hp and greater" = 350.0
)

hp_df <- imap_dfr(hp_data_list, ~ .x %>% mutate(hp_category = .y)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Texas", "Louisiana", "Mississippi", "Alabama", "Florida"),
               names_to = "state", values_to = "sales") %>%
  mutate(
    gulf_sales  = if_else(state == "Florida", sales * 0.50, sales),
    hp_midpoint = hp_midpoints[hp_category],
    speed_knots = 3.5 * sqrt(hp_midpoint),
    radius_nm   = speed_knots * 2
  )

milestone_years <- c(2011, 2016, 2021, 2024)

# GROUP BY YEAR AND STATE to isolate regional fleet profiles (>= 150 HP)
reach_milestones_by_state <- hp_df %>%
  filter(
    year %in% milestone_years,
    hp_midpoint >= 175  # 150–199.9 HP class and above (offshore-capable)
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, state) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_reach_nm = sum(radius_nm * gulf_sales, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(gulf_sales, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

nm_to_m <- 1852

# Build state-varying footprint bands for each milestone year
buffers_df <- map_dfr(milestone_years, function(yr) {
  # Get state-specific reach radii for the given year
  yr_data <- reach_milestones_by_state %>% filter(year == yr)
  
  # Buffer each state independently by its specific reach radius
  state_buffers <- map(1:nrow(yr_data), function(j) {
    st_name <- yr_data$state[j]
    dist_m  <- yr_data$avg_reach_nm[j] * nm_to_m
    
    # Get geometry for this state
    st_geom <- gulf_states %>% filter(name == st_name)
    
    # Create state-specific buffer
    st_buffer(st_geom, dist = dist_m)
  })
  
  # Union all state buffers for this milestone year into one seamless shape
  combined_yr_buf <- st_union(do.call(c, state_buffers))
  
  # Subtract land area
  buf_offshore <- st_difference(combined_yr_buf, st_union(gulf_states))
  
  # Intersect strictly with the official Gulf ocean polygon
  buf_gulf_only <- st_intersection(buf_offshore, gulf_ocean_poly)
  
  st_sf(
    year = as.factor(yr),
    geometry = st_geometry(buf_gulf_only)
  )
}) %>% 
  arrange(desc(year)) # Ensure largest/newest buffer renders underneath older ones

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Plot Map
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#e0f2f1")) +
  
  # Draw state-varying buffer bands clipped strictly to official Gulf ocean boundary
  geom_sf(data = buffers_df, aes(fill = year), color = "gray30", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_sf(data = gulf_states, fill = "#f4f4f2", color = "gray40", size = 0.4) +
  
  scale_fill_nmfs(
    palette = "complement_teal", 
    discrete = TRUE, 
    reverse = FALSE,
    name = "Milestone Year\n(Offshore Fleet Reach)"
  ) +
  
  # View Bounding Box
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-97.5, -81.0), 
    ylim = c(24.5, 31.0), 
    crs = st_crs(4326), 
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  
  # Shifted Scale Bar & North Arrow to Bottom Right (br)
  annotation_scale(
    location = "br", 
    width_hint = 0.25,
    pad_x = unit(1, "in"), 
    pad_y = unit(0.3, "in")
  ) +
  annotation_north_arrow(
    location = "br", 
    which_north = "true", 
    pad_x = unit(1, "in"), 
    pad_y = unit(0.5, "in"),
    style = north_arrow_minimal()
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Expansion of Offshore Reach in the Gulf by State Fleet Profile",
    subtitle = "Modeled 2-hour reach radius (≥150 HP) incorporating state-level horsepower distributions",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "white", size = 0.2)
  )
```

# 3. Save Formatted data as csv

This will save your data to the appropriate folder.
```{r}
write.csv(formatted_data, file = csv_filename, row.names = F)
```


# 4. Create Data_Prep object

Please use your formatted csv to create a "data_prep" object.
For more info on the data_prep function see the vignette linked above.
```{r}
data_obj<-IEAnalyzeR::data_prep(csv_filename, subind = "extent")
```

# 5. Save Formatted data_prep object

This will save your data to the appropriate folder.
```{r}
saveRDS(data_obj, file = object_filename)
```

# 6. Preview Plot

Use the IEAnalyzeR plotting function to preview the data.
This will not necessarily be the final figure used in reports.
For more info on the plot_fn_obj function go HERE

```{r}
IEAnalyzeR::plot_fn_obj(df_obj = data_obj, trend = TRUE, xbreaks_by = 2, ncol = 1)
```

# 7. Save plot

This will save the plot to the correct folder.
Adjust height & width using (height=, width=, unit="in") if needed.

```{r}
ggsave(filename = plot_filename)
```
